text:
**My pick: Jackery Solar Generator 1000 v2 with a 200W panel, about $699 (list $879).** It has 1,070Wh of LiFePO4 battery, 1,500W AC output, and a 1-hour fast charge from a wall outlet. It weighs about 23.8 lbs. It has 4.5 stars from 1.4K Amazon reviews, and Talk of the House also picks it as its editor's choice. [Find it on Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/solar-generator-panels-included/s?k=solar+generator+with+panels+included). The same review notes that the fast charge needs app activation, and that the panel may ship separately from the power station, so check that both arrive.

**Other good options, by need:**

| Need | Pick | Price (as listed) | Link |
|---|---|---|---|
| Similar size, strong alternatives | EcoFlow Delta 3 Classic + 220W panel (1,024Wh, 4.6 stars) | $699 (list $1,099) | [Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/solar-generator-panels/s?k=solar+generator+with+solar+panels) |
| | BLUETTI Elite 100 V2 + 200W panel (1,024Wh, 4.5 stars) | $699 (list $999) | [Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/solar-generator-panels/s?k=solar+generator+with+solar+panels) |
| Costco members | Jackery Explorer 1500 v2 with solar panel | $899.99 | [Costco](https://www.costco.com/home-solar-power.html) |
| Home backup (about 2 kWh) | Jackery Explorer 2000 v2 + 2x200W (4.6 stars) | $1,399 | [Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/solar-generator-panels-included/s?k=solar+generator+with+panels+included) |
| | BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 + 2x200W (4.7 stars) | $1,399 | [Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/solar-generator-panels/s?k=solar+generator+with+solar+panels) |
| Larger home backup (about 3 kWh) | BLUETTI Elite 300 + 2x200W (4.7 stars) | $1,599.99 | [Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/solar-generator-panels/s?k=solar+generator+with+solar+panels) |

**Which to choose:**
- **Camping, RV, or short outages:** a roughly 1 kWh kit like the Jackery 1000 v2 covers a fridge for several hours, CPAP machines, and electronics.
- **Longer outages or running a fridge overnight:** step up to the 2 kWh kits.
- **EcoFlow:** Top Consumer Reviews ranks it #1 overall for its UPS-speed switchover (10ms), expandability, and app ([review](https://www.topconsumerreviews.com/best-solar-generators/detailed-reviews.php)).

**Caveats:**
- The Amazon links go to search results pages, since those were the pages I could draw from. Look for the exact model name in the list.
- Prices are from today's listings and change often.
- Several of the Amazon results I saw were sponsored placements. I picked mainly on review counts, ratings, and the independent reviews.
- Cheaper no-name kits (for example the $180 300W bundle) have lower capacity, and I'd skip them for anything beyond charging phones.

If you tell me your budget and what you want to power, I can narrow it to one.
